title: The Weakest Dragon Emperor
text: That day, my Father was kept busy tending to the people from the eastern village. Even after recovering from his illness, he hadn’t fully regained his strength, so I prescribed him some supplementary medicine. I helped out a bit, too.
“Well, as for the rest… like purifying the contaminated land—I guess we’ll just have to leave that to the government folks.”
“That’s right.”

Cleansing the land contaminated by the dragon involves a lot of complicated procedures and requires purification Magic, you know. Well, I don’t know if they’ve done it in the future or not. The land has become shrouded in dark clouds, but other than that, there don’t seem to be any major problems. Once you get used to it, you almost start to take even an ominous sky in stride.

That night, a bonfire was lit in the center of the village, as if to celebrate the end of the plague. It was a modest little celebration. Father stayed up late discussing medication prescriptions with the healer.
“Phew… I’m exhausted.”

The Assistant was sitting quietly in a corner of the village with the monster. He was staring off into the distance toward the mountains, perhaps reflecting on the events of the day. Even the villagers, having learned their lesson, kept quiet and didn’t make a fuss. Father slumped back exhausted in a chair at the inn the village had prepared.
“Good job, big bro.”
“Good job, Naofumi.”
Keel and Sakura-chan brought Father some tea.
“Thank you.”
Father took a big sip of tea and let out a sigh.
“Well then… where’s Wyndia?”
“She’s exhausted and asleep. Hmm… I think I’ll turn in soon, too.”
“Good night, Keel.”
“Piyo!”

Luna went over to Keel, who was about to go to sleep, and it looks like she’s going to sleep with him. Yuki and Kou are sleeping outside. By the way, it’s not that they’re being left out. They’re sleeping out there of their own accord to guard the perimeter. That’s Filolial-sama for you.
“Well then, we’re setting off tomorrow. Given the time of year, maybe we should head down to the castle town for a bit.”
“That’s right. We’re getting close to the day we’re supposed to meet up with Ren.”

We’d agreed to meet up once about a month from now. We’ve decided to talk in Riyute Village when that time comes. I tend to forget these things, but my Father showed me the detailed schedule, so I remember it now.
“That’s true. Still, we’ve got a little more time.”
“All things considered, it’s a week before the Wave, isn’t it?”
“We decided on that because we figured Ren would be busy too. I wonder how things are going over there.”
“Zeltoble is one of the easier countries to live in. If you’re strong enough, you can make it work no matter what.”
It’s a country that even easily accepted that fallen Itsuki from the future. If it’s just a matter of living there, even we could manage it with ease.
“Is that so? I’d like to go there someday, though.”
“The local specialty is the Filolial Race!”
“Wow… that sounds like the kind of race Motoyasu-kun would like. All I can picture is horse racing.”
“Does your Father like it?”
“Hmm… I’ve played it in video games, but I’ve never seen it in real life.”
“I see.”
“Does Sakura race, too?”
Just as we were talking about the Filolial Races, Sakura-chan joined the conversation. I picture Sakura-chan dashing gracefully around the track. That would be an amazing moment.
“I don’t know. Maybe we should just decide when the time comes?”
“I see… Yuki would probably like that.”
“Yeah, Yuki-chan. She seems to take pride in running.”
“Come to think of it, we haven’t visited the Filolial breeder who sold us Yuki-chan and the others at all.”
“We’ve been pretty busy with everything. Should we go once the Melromarc incident is all wrapped up?”
“That sounds good. It’ll be a sight to see that breeder’s surprised face.”
Just then, we heard a knock on the window.
“Hm?”
When Father stepped up to the window, the monster that had been knocking… peeked its head inside.
“Gaelion-chan?”
When Father opened the window, the monster… shrank into a tiny form amid a faint glow and stepped inside the room.
“It seems you received some power from Wyndia-chan’s father and learned all sorts of skills.”
“Well, that’s how it goes.”
Father looked utterly dumbfounded upon hearing the voice of the monster Assistant speaking.
“I can’t blame you for being surprised. But I’d like you to hear me out. I have my own reasons for speaking to you like this.”
“Talking—”
“Gau! Oh, that’s right. Let me reintroduce myself. I am Gaelion. Well, it seems my step-sister—whom my daughter Wyndia named—shares the same name.”
“Daughter…?”
“That’s right. To the Shield Hero and the Spear Hero, I cannot thank you enough. Thank you for protecting and raising Wyndia.”
Flapping its wings—a monster… no, this is a dragon, Filo-tan’s Rival! No mistake about it! My arch-enemy!
“Father, it’s this guy! This is the dragon who helped her break through her limits and master the Way of the Dragon Vein in the future!”
“Eh… but Gaelion-chan… ah, is it because of that dragon’s Core Stone?”
“You’re mostly correct. I am Gaelion, one of the Dragon Emperors.”
“I’ve heard about you from Filo-tan. You’re the weakest of the Dragon Emperors, aren’t you?”
“That’s right. I am the weakest among the Dragon Emperors. That’s precisely why I made my lair near human settlements—a place the other Dragon Emperors wouldn’t dare approach.”
“I-I see… You admit you’re the weakest yourself…”
My father scratched his head with a look of exasperation. He really is a bit of a goofball. And he even admitted he’s weak himself. This is ridiculous—I can’t stop laughing.
“Hahahaha!”
“Motoyasu-kun, I’ll admit it’s funny, but you’re laughing way too much.”
My Father scolded me. But I simply can’t help but laugh at this. I’m going to laugh as hard as I possibly can. For such a weakling to be Filo-tan’s Rival… it’s truly lamentable.

“Anyway, let’s get back to the topic. Thanks to that dragon zombie from earlier today giving Gaelion-chan the glowing stone on her chest, all sorts of changes happened—but what exactly was that phenomenon? Did you, as her parent, take over your child’s consciousness?”
“That’s not it. I’m merely sharing my personality and memories with my daughter’s body. She remains the owner of that body.”
“Huh… So this is a real-life gender swap… or maybe not quite…”
“Now that she’s gained power, she’ll probably start talking any minute now. You’d better look forward to it.”
I’m not exactly thrilled about this. Come to think of it, I don’t recall Gaelion from the first world ever speaking. Hah! Could it be… that he was just catering to my Father’s tastes!?

I remember my Father saying something like, “Pets are fine as long as they don’t talk.” In fact, among the Filolial-sama who lived in the village, there were some who could talk but pretended they couldn’t.
Ugh… How despicable, Dragon. Were the Filolial-sama doing that too? But the Filolial-sama are fine!
“Ah… well, at least it saves us the trouble of having Wyndia-chan translate for us. So, what do you want from us?”
“Hmm. Thanks to this shared state, I’ve been able to see various memories through my daughter’s eyes. Now then, you may already know this, but—”
“I don’t know what?”
“I want to become stronger. And your cooperation is essential for me to become stronger. So, I’d like to formally ask for your continued cooperation.”
“Ah… yeah. I get that, but aren’t you Wyndia-chan’s foster parent? Since she’s effectively come back to life, aren’t you going to talk to her? I’m sure she’d be happy.”

“……That’s a cruel request. You see… I’ve always wanted that child to eventually set out into the human world on her own. In a sense, this is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. You must not tell her that I’ve ended up returning like this. It wouldn’t be in her best interest.”

My rival shared the story of the Assistant’s background. A group of Demi-Human merchants was attacked by bandits, and the Assistant’s parents—unaware that my rival was a dragon—entrusted their infant daughter to him. Since then, my rival has acted as a surrogate parent to her, and she has become his irreplaceable daughter.

“After all, no matter how hard she tries, that child cannot survive in the world of dragons. She must learn about the human world and make her way there. If she knows I’m watching over her from close by… it’ll only hinder her growth.”
My father sat down in his chair and fell deep in thought.
“I wonder if that’s really how it is…”

I just can’t accept that. It’s so sad that even if they’re dragons, parents and children can’t live in the same time. If that’s the case, there’s no reason to put up with this little brat’s selfishness.
“Then I’ll go wake up my Assistant and explain the situation to her!”
